reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: An outstanding residency
reviews.body:
An outstanding residency. Studios are mind-blowing (mine had a baby grand piano!), privacy/quietude is perfect, food was so much better that I had expected. Check out the amazing library--which contains thousands of works done by previous and current MacDowell residents. The staff is top-notch: friendly, very helpful, and they kept it all together beautifully when the electric cut out during a three-foot blizzard.

— Anonymous, 2023. Imported from the original ratemyartistresidency.com archive.

callInfo.name: Fall/Winter 2027 Fellowship
callInfo.description: MacDowell Fellowships support artists across all disciplines with exclusive studio use, private accommodations, and meals for up to eight weeks. Selection is based solely on artistic excellence.

callInfo.name: Winter 2026 Application Cycle (May 2027 – March 2028)
callInfo.description: Yaddo's winter cycle closes December 20, 2026 (11:59pm ET) for residencies beginning May 2027 through March 2028 — note the date moved from the old early-January deadline. The application portal typically opens mid-November; $35 nonrefundable fee. Residencies of two weeks to two months on the Saratoga Springs estate are free to those admitted: private studios, room, and board.

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: Concerns raised by a former resident (unverified)
reviews.body:
An anonymous reviewer described an uncomfortable welcome, recounting interactions with a member of the program's leadership that they found culturally insensitive, and said staff indicated such behavior was not isolated. They also noted that a studio-placement request to be near a collaborator went unhonored, and felt the program's culture leaned more social and 'vacation'-oriented than work-focused, which did not fit their goals. One unverified first-hand account.

— Anonymous, 2015. Imported f

reviews.name: Perfectly adequate -- Not really for writers though
reviews.body: Perfectly adequate -- Not really for writers though. Organizational quality is low. It is rather inefficiently run by other artists, who do not have a sense of business. For example, asked if I could make arrangements to send my books back home after the residency and I was told to leave a BLANK CHECK at the office and they would later fill in the amount to send the items back. They couldn't even provide an estimate on what it would cost. Here's a suggestion - on the last day, offer to get a van

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: I stayed at Vermont Studio Center for three consecutive months
reviews.body: I stayed at Vermont Studio Center for three consecutive months. It was my first residency experience and I had the time of my life. I have attended six art residencies since then and VSC was by far the most social, interactive, academic... and expensive. The available work/study arrangements and financial aid are appreciated, but even still this is an expensive retreat. However, you do get your money's worth, since there are lectures, visiting artists, exhibitions, a library, networking galore,

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: I took part in a four week residency at VSC in 2015
reviews.body: I took part in a four week residency at VSC in 2015. It is expensive but I saved up for this and it was worth it. It meant all the difference to have a place to sleep, 3 meals a day prepared for you, and visiting artists that did studio visits. Everyone was very dedicated to their work while I was there which was very motivating, I made so much work. At the time I really needed a space free from distractions and due to the amount of snow we got at the time it made it that much easier to focus on

callInfo.name: Summer/Fall 2027 Residency
callInfo.description: VSC's fall application window (August 15 – September 30, 2026) fills 2-, 3-, and 4-week residencies running roughly late June through mid-December 2027. Every admitted resident receives at least a partial fellowship and about a third attend on full fellowships; international applicants are welcome and receive visa support letters. Confirm the exact window dates on the apply page when it opens.

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: I'm a writer who did an 18 day residency here in the summer
reviews.body: I'm a writer who did an 18 day residency here in the summer. Bikes available to ride to the nearby lake. Attentive staff who leave you at peace. Quiet atmosphere. I had one of the best bedroom/studios so I have no complaints. Some of the other bedrooms were much smaller. Two houses, one renovated, one not. Some had screened in porches they wrote in. Food supplies for breakfast/lunch are somewhat lackluster and sparse. Dinner is communal and the food was decent. You can buy your own groceries, th

callInfo.name: Ragdale 2028 Residency Program
callInfo.description: Ragdale provides a supportive community and uninterrupted time on an 80-acre prairie sanctuary north of Chicago. Residencies of 18 days; up to 165 residencies awarded annually. Eleven named fellowships include a $1,000+ stipend and waived fee. Single annual deadline covers all 2028 sessions. Notifications sent in September; final packets with session dates in October.

callInfo.name: Fall 2027 Residency
callInfo.description: Ucross runs two annual deadlines: January 15 for the following fall session and July 15 for the following spring. Applications for the Fall 2027 season (August through early December 2027) open November 1, 2026 and close January 15, 2027 — two- to six-week fully hosted stays with housing, studios, and meals on a 20,000-acre Wyoming ranch. Confirm the window on Submittable when it opens.

callInfo.name: 2027 Civitella Ranieri Fellowship
callInfo.description: The Civitella Ranieri Fellowship supports artists and writers for 5-week residencies at a 15th-century Umbrian castle in Italy. All costs covered including international travel. Highly competitive: approximately 15 fellows selected from 1,000+ applicants.

callInfo.name: Core Residency: April–July 2027
callInfo.description: Millay Arts' October 1, 2026 deadline fills Core Residency sessions April through July 2027 at Steepletop, Edna St. Vincent Millay's former Hudson Valley home. Residencies are fully subsidized — housing, studio, groceries, and chef-prepared dinners — with a $100 deposit on acceptance. A late-application window runs through October 8 at a higher fee.

callInfo.name: Summer 2027 Artist-in-Residence
callInfo.description: Anderson Ranch's 8-week summer residency in Snowmass Village, Colorado. Fully equipped studios for ceramics, woodworking, painting, printmaking, photography, and sculpture. Housing provided; merit scholarships available. Annual application deadline falls around mid-February.

name: Virginia Center for the Creative Arts (VCCA)

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: The studios were sunny and clean (although, not so clean that you had
reviews.body: The studios were sunny and clean (although, not so clean that you had to worry about accidentally leaving a mark). The food was pretty ok - it's always nice to go to a residency where they cook for you, so you don't have to waste precious time on food prep/shopping. There was a continuous stream of people (about 1/2 of those present) who had been to this residency before (many several times), which was interesting. The living quarters are aging, but clean. I was able to complete a lot of work wh

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: I found VCCA a peaceful, lovely place to get a lot of work done
reviews.body: I found VCCA a peaceful, lovely place to get a lot of work done. It's not grand, but it's nice and well-run, with serious, high-quality colleagues. The grounds are well-groomed, mostly graceful open space. The food is basic and somewhat heavy (not health food). The bedrooms all have lovely views but no sonic privacy (all rooms have open spaces above their doors, due to the design of the heating / air conditioning system, which can't be individually controlled; I found the AC freezing cold). FYI,

reviews.body:
The photos on this page are not of VCCA and are frankly nicer than VCCA - would be good to correct this

— Anonymous, 2018. Imported from the original ratemyartistresidency.com archive.

callInfo.name: Summer 2027 Fellowship
callInfo.description: VCCA offers 2–8 week fellowships in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Private studio, bedroom, and three meals a day. No application fee and no residency fee — supported entirely by donations and grants. VCCA reviews on three fixed deadlines a year: January 15, May 15, and September 15.

callInfo.name: 2027 Skowhegan Session
callInfo.description: Skowhegan's nine-week summer session runs June 5 – August 7, 2027 on the school's 350-acre Maine campus. Applications open September 1, 2026 and are reported to close October 16, 2026 — confirm the exact close date when the portal opens. Tuition-based with substantial need-based financial aid; international participants accepted.

callInfo.name: 2027 Residency Program
callInfo.description: 4–5 week residencies on 583 acres in the Santa Cruz Mountains. Private studio, room, and board provided at no cost. One of the few fully-funded programs on the West Coast.

callInfo.name: July–December 2027 Residency (General Application)
callInfo.description: The general application for July–December 2027 sessions opens September 1, 2026 and closes November 1, 2026. Unlike the early-application track, general applicants are eligible for financial aid and fully funded fellowships. Two- or four-week stays with private studios inside the MASS MoCA campus, shared housing, and an open-studio community of up to ten artists at a time.

callInfo.name: Winter/Spring 2027 Residency
callInfo.description: 2–4 week residencies in the Maine Highlands. Private studio and housing provided. Monson is a small community that has re-centered its identity around the arts. Three review deadlines a year: January 15, May 15, and September 15.

name: Atlantic Center for the Arts
location: New Smyrna Beach, FL, United States

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: ACA was absolutely one of the best times of my life as an artist
reviews.body: ACA was absolutely one of the best times of my life as an artist. They feed you, they house you, they provide you a mentor, and they give you all the space and supplies you necessary to work. On top of all that, they do a lot of the legwork to get grants and make the residency as affordable as possible. You will meet people from all around the world who work in different creative fields, and the collaborations you make will be incredible. I got to work with visual artists, poets, and opera compo

callInfo.name: 2027–2028 Camargo Core Program Fellowship
callInfo.description: The Camargo Core Program awards 14 fully funded fellowships a year — seven to artists, seven to scholars and thinkers — for ten-week stays on the foundation's clifftop campus in Cassis, France, with housing and a stipend. The 2027–2028 cycle offers sessions September 8 – November 17, 2027 or February 23 – May 4, 2028. Applications close October 1, 2026 at 23:59 CET; open to all nationalities.

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: Concerns raised by a former resident (unverified)
reviews.body:
An anonymous reviewer described a controlling management style and limited staff autonomy, and said other former residents shared negative experiences. On facilities: studios were described as noisy and poorly maintained, with little shared space and few resources offered to artists (for example, artists asked to supply their own materials). This is one unverified first-hand account.

— Anonymous, 2025. Imported from the original ratemyartistresidency.com archive.

callInfo.name: International Residency Program (Rolling Admissions)
callInfo.description: NARS accepts rolling applications year-round from internationally based artists for three-, six-, and twelve-month Brooklyn residencies aligned to quarterly seasons, with decisions in three to four weeks ($35 fee; 2026 program fees from $9,900 for three months). US-based artists apply instead through bi-annual spring and fall open calls, which include one full fellowship covering program fees — the fall window historically runs mid-August to mid-September. Confirm current portal status on the apply page.

callInfo.name: 2027–2028 Fellowship Program
callInfo.description: 6–12 month fellowship at Kala's printmaking and media arts facility in Berkeley. Access to lithography, etching, screen printing, letterpress, darkroom, and digital labs. Monthly stipend for fellows. Applications open around mid-December and close March 1.

callInfo.name: Rolling Fellowship
callInfo.description: 4-week residency on the wild Atlantic coast of County Mayo, Ireland. Private studio with views of the bay. Housing provided. A contemplative setting for deep creative focus. Applications are accepted year-round and reviewed twice yearly; a €50 fee applies for international artists.

callInfo.name: Institut français x Cité internationale des arts 2027
callInfo.description: Three-, six-, or nine-month Paris residencies between April 2027 and April 2028 for artists and cultural professionals who have lived outside France for five-plus years, all disciplines, with a minimum monthly grant of €1,100 plus travel, insurance, and visa support. Note the eligibility mechanics: applications must be filed by a partner organization (such as the local French cultural network), not directly by the artist. Deadline October 8, 2026.

name: Ox-Bow School of Art and Artists' Residency

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: Very pleased with the experience
reviews.body: I just finished a 2 week fall residency and was very pleased with the experience. It was a nice number of artists (about 20) and they were from all over (several from Chicago due to the SAIC connection). The facilities were great - the living quarters are relatively new, and they do a good job of keeping everything clean and functioning. The beach was great (can hike or canoe there). The food was excellent - good quality and lots of variety. Good price for what you get. I would recommend it to a

callInfo.name: Slow Season Residency (Rolling Applications)
callInfo.description: Ox-Bow's self-directed Slow Season residencies run in two- to four-week stays during September–November 2026 and March–April 2027 on the Saugatuck, Michigan campus. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis via a Submittable portfolio inquiry, open to artists of all levels and disciplines. Costs run $1,200 for one week up to $4,200 for four, including a private dorm-style room, weeknight dinners, and a stocked pantry.

name: Sitka Center for Art and Ecology

reviews.author: Erin Noel
reviews.name: Great spot and people!
reviews.body: The housing was wonderful, studio extremely accommodating to many media. I worked on a series of mono prints as well as some paintings.

callInfo.name: 2026–2027 Long-Term Residency
callInfo.description: 1–3 year residency for ceramic artists on a 26-acre historic brickyard in Helena, Montana. Private studio, subsidized housing, and access to extensive clay and glaze facilities. One of the world's premier ceramics programs.

callInfo.name: 2027–2029 Core Fellowship
callInfo.description: Penland's Core Fellowship is a 3-year residency for emerging craft artists. Fellows work in clay, glass, iron, metals, fibers, print, photography, or wood. Private studio, housing, meals, stipend, and access to all workshops.

callInfo.name: 2027 Residencies: Hauberg Fellowship & Innovation in Image
callInfo.description: Pilchuck's annual residency deadlines: the John H. Hauberg Fellowship (a collaborative residency for a group of up to six cross-media artists) and the Innovation in Image Residency are due December 18, 2026, and the Emerging Artist in Residence program (glass experience required) closes January 15, 2027 — recurring annual dates; confirm on the apply page when the cycle posts. Residencies take place at the Stanwood, WA campus in 2027.

callInfo.name: Summer 2027 Open Studio Residency
callInfo.description: 2-week open studio residency at Haystack's iconic Edward Larrabee Barnes–designed campus on Deer Isle, Maine. Self-directed access to studios in ceramics, fibers, graphics, metals, wood, and glass. Applications typically open in early January and close in early February.

name: Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity

callInfo.name: Write Over Here: Indigenous Futurism Residency 2027
callInfo.description: This program welcomes Indigenous screenwriters at various stages of their careers to apply individually or with a collaborator to work on adapting their work for the screen. Collaborators may include novelists, short story writers, or playwrights. The program supports writers who want to advance their work and are exploring themes of futurism for film and television adaptations. This residency balances self-directed writing in personal studios and scheduled workshops, discussions, and events. Participants will refine their screenwriting skills, collaborate with peers, and engage in culturally informed creative practices. Online preparatory week: Intro sessions, script reviews and one-on-one sessions to prepare participants fully for the on-campus program weeks. Faculty and guest artist led workshops covering story and character development, screenwriting techniques, and creative practice. Peer-to-peer engagement and collaborative exercises. One-on-one consultations with faculty

callInfo.name: Collective Creation Laboratory 2027: Walking as Method
callInfo.description: A thematic collective residency at the foot of Montserrat exploring walking as an artistic and research methodology, with a October 3, 2026 application deadline; session dates and fees are being finalized — confirm on the official call page. Can Serrat's separate rolling residency route also accepts applications year-round (self-funded, full value around €2,089/month; grants attach only to dated calls).

callInfo.name: Spring 2027 Thematic Residency
callInfo.description: 2–4 week residency in a renovated school in rural Finland. Focus on mindfulness, sustainability, and creative process. Sauna included. Surrounded by Finnish lake country. Arteles runs several thematic cycles a year; the next deadline is expected around late November.

reviews.body: I loved the private rooms/bathrooms at this residency. The shared kitchen became a sticking point at times when people bickered over washing dishes/emptying the dishwasher or tried to juggle multiple people trying to make a meal at the same time. The open-air courtyard was an excellent place to relax or eat a meal, especially at the time of year I went (June 2012). Getting groceries was a trick because there's a wall separating the the parking lots between SFAI and the grocery store, so you had

reviews.body: A bit of Skowhegan lite, great artists- really international, not just the usual Germany and Japan. I was there with artists from Cuba, Mexico, Nigeria, China, Chile. Brazil, all over Europe and the United States that I am still in touch with. The owner is a brilliant eccentric, housing is newish, beautiful area. One of the best aspect is all the studio visits (one of the few residencies that does this), they bring in galleries, critics, and curators the duration of the residency. The barn is wi

callInfo.name: Art Omi: Artists 2027 Residency
callInfo.description: Art Omi's flagship residency gathers roughly two dozen international artists plus visiting critics and curators in Ghent, NY for a fully hosted session June 17 – July 12, 2027 (room, board, and studio covered). The application window runs August 14 – September 14, 2026 with a $15 fee; applicants need five-plus years of demonstrated practice. Notification the following March.

callInfo.name: 2027 Artist Residency
callInfo.description: 8-month residency in a converted grain elevator in the Hudson Valley. Free studio space including massive former grain silos.

callInfo.name: 2027–2028 Residency
callInfo.description: One-year post-academic residency with monthly stipend, private studio, and access to exceptional production facilities. Renewable for a second year.

callInfo.name: 2027 Artist Residency
callInfo.description: 2–3 month residency on a campus outside New Delhi with three museums (terracotta, textiles, everyday art). Studio and accommodation provided. Immersion in India's living craft traditions.

callInfo.name: Rolling International Fellowships
callInfo.description: Gasworks runs multiple partner- and region-specific fellowships throughout the year for artists from Africa, Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America — each a fully funded 3-month London residency with studio, accommodation, living allowance, and production budget. There is no single annual deadline; check the Opportunities page for the call that is currently open.

callInfo.name: 2027 Residencies Programme
callInfo.description: 3-month research-focused residency at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore. Stipend, housing, studio, production budget, and access to NTU labs.

callInfo.name: 2027 International Residency
callInfo.description: 3-month discursive residency in Rio de Janeiro. Accommodation, stipend, and intensive curatorial programming. Emphasis on discussion, theory, and collaborative practice.

callInfo.name: 2027 La Práctica Residency
callInfo.description: 6-month residency in Old San Juan for artists, writers, curators, and activists. Studio, $500/month stipend, weekly seminars, and deep engagement with Puerto Rican culture.

callInfo.name: Proposal-Based Residency (Rolling)
callInfo.description: Alice Yard, the Port of Spain artist-run space active since 2008 (and a documenta fifteen lumbung member), hosts visiting artists and curators on an informal, proposal-based model: email a CV and short project proposal to arrange a stay of a few days to a few months. Visits are generally self-funded or self-arranged, with funded routes occasionally available through partner projects.

callInfo.name: Rolling Residency in La Plata
callInfo.description: Residencia Corazón — running since 2006 — accepts rolling applications year-round from artists of all nationalities and disciplines for stays of two weeks to two-plus months in La Plata, Argentina, with a seven-day response time. Self-funded at roughly US$800–1,500 depending on program and length, with 2026 discounts for month-plus stays, shared rooms, and collectives; the residency issues invitation letters for mobility-fund applications (DAAD, Pro Helvetia, Canada Council, and similar).

callInfo.name: 2027 International Residency
callInfo.description: 1–3 month residency on the Tamsui River in suburban Taipei. Site-specific and environmental art focus. Studio, accommodation, and small stipend provided.

callInfo.name: Greatmore Studios Visiting Artist Residency (Rolling)
callInfo.description: 2–3 month visiting artist residency in Cape Town's Woodstock neighborhood. Private studio alongside 20+ permanent South African studio holders. Three intake periods per year: Jan–Mar, May–Jul, Sep–Nov. Apply by emailing biography, CV, motivation letter, and images to info@greatmoreart.org.

callInfo.name: 2027 Artist-in-Residence
callInfo.description: 2–3 month residency in forested northern Honshu. Studio, accommodation, ¥150,000/month stipend, and access to wood/metal workshops. Community engagement focus.

callInfo.name: 2028 Residency Programme
callInfo.description: 2–5 month residency on the Curonian Spit, a UNESCO-listed sand dune peninsula on the Baltic coast. Studio, accommodation, and €500/month stipend. Ecological art and interdisciplinary research focus. Nida runs a single annual open call with a deadline around 31 March.

callInfo.name: Rolling Self-Funded Residency
callInfo.description: 1–3 month self-funded residency in Beijing's 798 Art District. Private studio, accommodation, Mandarin lessons, and curated studio visits. Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis — contact the program directly to arrange dates.

callInfo.name: Artist Residency (Rolling Applications)
callInfo.description: The Swatch Art Peace Hotel hosts artists of all disciplines for three- to six-month stays in Shanghai with free live/work space, round-trip travel organized and paid by the host, visa invitation letters, and up to CHF 300 toward visa costs (no stipend). Applications are accepted year-round — allow a minimum of twelve weeks for review — with a CHF 30 application fee donated to Médecins Sans Frontières.

callInfo.name: International Residency Program (Rolling Applications)
callInfo.description: ISCP's core international residency has no fixed deadline — applications are reviewed year-round on a rolling basis, with no application fee. Residents are self-funded or sponsored by foundations, cultural ministries, and partner institutions; 2026 studio rates run roughly $2,600–$2,900/month depending on studio size. ISCP also posts fully funded sponsored open calls (with their own deadlines) throughout the year — watch the apply page.

callInfo.name: 2027 Mudhouse Residency
callInfo.description: Two- to four-week residency in a restored stone house in the village of Agios Ioannis on Crete, Greece. Small cohorts of writers, visual artists, photographers, choreographers, composers. Family-style meals.

callInfo.name: 2027 Writers in Residence
callInfo.description: 2–6 week residency for women-identifying, non-binary, and gender non-conforming writers. Private cottage, meals, and travel stipend. All genres welcome.

callInfo.name: Spring 2027 Residency
callInfo.description: 2–8 week residency in the Blue Ridge Mountains. Private studio cottage on 600 forested acres. Fellowships cover full residency fee for qualifying artists. The application window for the spring session runs August 1 through September 15.

callInfo.name: Parque Residency Program (Rolling Admissions)
callInfo.description: Casa Lü reviews applications on a rolling basis for month-long cohorts running throughout 2026 at its Tlalpan, Mexico City site (sessions close as cohorts fill — they advise applying six to twelve months ahead; responses in two weeks to a month, finalists interviewed). Primarily visual artists, other disciplines welcome. The residency is fee-based with partial scholarships available as fee reductions on request — confirm current rates when applying.

callInfo.name: 2027 Residency Programme
callInfo.description: 2–3 month residency in Todd Saunders–designed studios on the coast of Newfoundland. Fully funded: travel, housing, studio, meals, and materials budget.

callInfo.name: July–December 2027 Residency (apply in December 2026)
callInfo.description: SÍM accepts applications only during two fixed windows each year. The next window runs December 1–31, 2026 for residencies taking place July–December 2027. Self-directed, self-funded stays of one to three months in Reykjavík at €500–850/month depending on the space.

callInfo.name: 2027 Art & Ecology Residency
callInfo.description: 2–4 week residency at the edge of Paljakka old-growth forest. Artists and scientists exploring ecological questions. Housing and meals provided.

callInfo.name: 2027 CULTIVATE Residency
callInfo.description: 4–8 week residency for composers at Aaron Copland's National Historic Landmark home. Steinway piano, private room, meals, and stipend.

callInfo.name: 2027 Season Residency
callInfo.description: Avaloch Farm hosts chamber ensembles, composers, conductors, soloists, and dance/theater/experimental projects for tuition-free residencies in Boscawen, New Hampshire — living accommodations, studio space, and all meals included. Applications for the 2027 season (via Acceptd) are due January 31, 2027; the application typically opens around December 1. Confirm the window when it posts.

callInfo.name: 2028–2029 Residency
callInfo.description: 2-year post-academic residency. Private studio (50–100 sqm), €1,500/month stipend, production budget, and access to world-class workshops. ~50 artists from 30+ countries.

callInfo.name: 2027–2028 International Residency
callInfo.description: 2–6 month residency in central Stockholm. Furnished studio-apartment, SEK 15,000/month stipend, and access to Swedish art institutions. International artists cannot self-apply — they must be nominated by a peer or curator; the annual proposal deadline is December 5.

callInfo.name: International Studio Programme (Partner-Organisation Applications)
callInfo.description: Bethanien has no single central deadline: its 12-month Berlin residencies — studio, apartment, roughly €1,500/month via national bursaries, and a final exhibition — are filled through partner organisations in a dozen-plus countries, each running its own annual call (examples: Norway in early February, New Zealand in early March, Greece July 1, Iceland early September). Artists without a partner organisation may apply directly if they bring secured independent funding. Check your country's partner for the next deadline.

callInfo.name: 2027 Residency Programme
callInfo.description: 6–12 month residency in Brussels alongside major exhibitions at WIELS contemporary art center. Studio, living allowance, and production budget.

callInfo.name: Medialab Matadero 2027: Situated Research Residencies
callInfo.description: Matadero's next open cycle is the Medialab situated-research programme: residencies running January–July 2027 for projects at the intersection of art, design, science, technology, and society, with a €10,000 gross stipend. Applications close September 27, 2026. No new El Ranchito cycle has been announced yet.

callInfo.name: Open Residencies (Rolling) — Funded Call Expected Autumn 2026
callInfo.description: Cove Park's Open Residencies accept applications year-round for self-funded stays of three nights to four months on its Scottish coastal site (single-occupancy cubes roughly £550–750/week; artists typically bring institutional or trust funding; no application fee). The next fully funded general call — for residencies April 2027 through December 2028, open to all art forms and career stages internationally — is expected in autumn 2026; watch the site.

callInfo.name: Graduate Residency 2027
callInfo.description: 6–8 week residency in a 13th-century estate on Scotland's Angus coast. Funded by Creative Scotland — free for accepted artists. Studios, printmaking workshop, and meals. The Graduate Residency open call closes November 2, 2026; other 2027 strands are posted on the opportunities page.

callInfo.name: Annaghmakerrig Residencies (Rolling Applications)
callInfo.description: The Tyrone Guthrie Centre at Annaghmakerrig reviews applications year-round for one- to two-week full-board residencies — all disciplines and career stages, open to artists in Ireland, Northern Ireland, Britain, and Europe. The subsidized rate is €490/week including all meals and studio access, and numerous county council and arts-organization bursaries cover the fee in full — check your local authority.

callInfo.name: 2027 Artist in Residence
callInfo.description: 2–3 month residency in Marfa, TX alongside Donald Judd's permanent installations. Housing, studio, and stipend in the Chihuahuan Desert.

callInfo.name: Visiting Artist Residency (Rolling Applications)
callInfo.description: 18th Street's Visiting Artist Residency accepts applications on a rolling basis, reviewed quarterly, for one- to three-month stays in one of four live/work studios in Santa Monica. Studios are subsidized (roughly $1–2 per square foot per month); many international residents arrive through cooperative agreements with cultural ministries and partner organizations, and funding is arranged case by case.

reviews.name: The Anderson Center at Tower View has, for me, become the golden

Their vision and practices for supporting the arts to create a better world is an inspiration to me, and has shifted my thinking as both an artist/writer as well as a fellow supporter of the arts. callInfo.name: 2027 Residency
callInfo.description: 2–4 week residency on the Mississippi River bluffs in Red Wing, MN. Private studio, housing, and meals. 6–8 residents per session. The annual application deadline falls around mid-January.

callInfo.name: Winter/Spring 2027 Residency
callInfo.description: Jentel hosts three-week residencies on a working cattle ranch outside Banner, Wyoming, with private accommodations, dedicated studio space, and a stipend toward living expenses. The September 15, 2026 deadline covers January–April 2027 sessions ($30 application fee). The following cycle (Summer/Fall 2027) opens October 1, 2026 and closes January 15, 2027.

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: Funky, weird, and fun, Art Farm provides a rural backdrop for your
reviews.body: Funky, weird, and fun, Art Farm provides a rural backdrop for your creative endeavors. For over 20 years, Artist Ed Dadey has kept these acres of misfit buildings and piles of surplus as a safe haven for the artist who seeks to enter a community and roll up their sleeves to keep it going. Participating artists (up to 12 at a time) agree to work for 12 hours a week to improve the place in return for your own room, studio, and access to a myriad supply of tools and materials. If you can find them.

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: Not for the faint of heart but for the free of spirit, Art Farm is
reviews.body: Not for the faint of heart but for the free of spirit, Art Farm is one of the last places of it's kind on earth. If you want permission to be your wildest, to experiment, to fail, to hands on learn a new trade, to fold quiet in your hands, to wander restored prairie, to discover the remnants of decades of artists, if you believe in the old, if you fix your shoes instead of buying new ones, if you long for a version of you driven by spirit and not by productivity, Art Farm may be for you. In deep

callInfo.name: Summer 2027 Residency
callInfo.description: Work-exchange summer residency on a Nebraska farm property. Visual artists, writers, and performers exchange roughly 12 hours/week of work for studio time, housing, and meals. Annual deadline March 1.

callInfo.name: 2027 HIAP International Residency
callInfo.description: 1–3 month residency on Suomenlinna sea fortress island in Helsinki. Studio-apartment, monthly grant, and access to HIAP's extensive international network. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

callInfo.name: 2027 Year-Long Residency
callInfo.description: A full year of funded studio time in Roswell, New Mexico, for six visual artists. Each receives a house with attached studio, all utilities, a monthly living stipend, and a materials stipend. No teaching or exhibition obligations. Annual deadline: March 15.

callInfo.name: 2027–2028 Studio Residency Grant
callInfo.description: A 6–8 week studio residency in intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or photography in Rosendale, NY. Weekly stipend, materials and travel support, free housing, and 24/7 studio access. Open to artists at any career stage.

callInfo.name: 2027 Sculpture Residency
callInfo.description: A two-month residency for sculptors in Utica, NY, with substantial financial support and private housing near the 7,000-square-foot studio. Four cohorts run February through November. Annual deadline: January 15.

callInfo.name: 2027 Filmmaker Residency
callInfo.description: A funded residency in Dawson City, Yukon, for filmmakers and media artists, run each spring alongside the Dawson City film festival. Private studio and accommodation in the historic Macaulay Residence at no cost. Deadline ~December 15.

callInfo.name: Rolling Residency (1–6 months)
callInfo.description: A multidisciplinary residency in the fishing town of Skagaströnd, north Iceland, open to all fields and career stages. Stays of one to six months; applications accepted year-round. Self-funded.

callInfo.name: Rolling Art & Ecology Residency
callInfo.description: An off-grid, climate-positive residency on 20 hectares in Andalusia's Sierra María-Los Vélez natural park. One- to two-week placements with private studio, accommodation, and all meals. Applications accepted year-round.

callInfo.name: Fall 2027 / Spring 2028 Fellowship
callInfo.description: One-month residential fellowships in a Ligurian fishing village near Genoa, across the arts and humanities. Living quarters, private workspace, and full board provided. Fall deadline ~November 25; Spring deadline ~March 6.

callInfo.name: Rolling Studio Residency
callInfo.description: Space-available studio residencies at Newtown Castle in the Burren, County Clare. Two-, four-, and twelve-week options with access to 3D, print, darkroom, and lighting studios. Accommodation arranged separately. Applications accepted year-round.

callInfo.name: 2027 Residency — December 2026 Application Round
callInfo.description: Youkobo runs two fixed application rounds a year, with deadlines June 30 (results in August) and December 31 (results in February). The December 31, 2026 round fills 2027 residency slots. Stays run one to twelve months (priority to two months or longer), all disciplines and nationalities; the residency is self-funded with monthly studio and accommodation fees and no application fee.

callInfo.name: Rolling International Residency
callInfo.description: A residency in Cali, Colombia, for artists, curators, writers, and cultural agents. Six-week minimum stay with a private room and shared work spaces; residents lead workshops and connect with local practitioners. Permanent open call.

name: Kimmel Harding Nelson Center for the Arts

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: I was a resident there a few years ago
reviews.body:
I was a resident there a few years ago. In my opinion, the facilities are sparse and outdated and the staff is a little conservative-minded. All that said, if you're looking for a residency that can provide space and time in a very small-town setting, KHN can be good.

— Anonymous, 2013. Imported from the original ratemyartistresidency.com archive.

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: I had a great experience at the KHN Center
reviews.body:
I had a great experience at the KHN Center. The staff were friendly and helpful. It's a great place for someone hoping for a quiet place to focus on work. Nebraska City is relatively rural and yet has a more museums than cities many times its size. Overall I would describe this residency as a nice midwest experience with friendly people and a relaxed atmosphere. I would highly recommend it.

— Anonymous, 2014. Imported from the original ratemyartistresidency.com archive.

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: I had an absolutely phenomenal experience at the KHN Center
reviews.body: I had an absolutely phenomenal experience at the KHN Center. The staff couldn't have been more helpful, friendly, or accommodating. They do everything within their power to provide a warm, relaxed atmosphere that is very conducive to work. I wrote so much more music than I expected to, and I also had a lot of fun. reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: The staff is very kind and informative, and the town of Nebraska City
reviews.body: The staff is very kind and informative, and the town of Nebraska City is a treasure to explore for inspiration. The summer can be a tad humid, but the spaciousness of the living space and a separate artist's working space makes KHN a fantastic site to create your works on. I was able to engage my work on all hours of the day and night. Only distraction I had was that the neighbors in the alley can be quite rowdy, so I would recommend wearing noise cancelling headphones if you choose to work late

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist

reviews.body: KHN was a perfect residency for me. I found the ideal balance between time to focus on my work and social interactions & small town distractions if needed. The director and her assistant are two incredibly friendly women.They create a relaxed and appreciative atmosphere and couldn't be more helpful. callInfo.name: 2027 KHN Residency Cycle
callInfo.description: Two- to eight-week residencies in Nebraska City, NE, for visual artists, writers, composers, choreographers, and scholars. Private studio and apartment, $100/week stipend, communal kitchen. Hosts ~70 artists/year. Annual deadline March 1.

callInfo.name: Year-Round Residency (Rolling Admissions)
callInfo.description: An artist-run residency in Laugarvatn, rural South Iceland, open to creative people of any discipline. Applications are accepted year-round; minimum stay is one month. Self-funded, with accommodation and a shared workspace; families can sometimes be accommodated.

callInfo.name: Residency Award — March 2027 Panel
callInfo.description: The second of Cill Rialaig's two annual selection rounds. Same terms as the September panel: individual cottage studios on Bolus Head for one to four weeks, no rental charge, €125/week toward utilities and waste disposal, and a €40 non-refundable application fee that must be received by close of business on March 15. Applications go by email to cillrialaigarts@gmail.com only. Summer and Christmas/New Year periods are the most heavily oversubscribed, and placements from this panel run into 2028.

reviews.name: GlogauAIR Long story short- it's worth it to be uncomfortable at
reviews.body: GlogauAIR Long story short- it's worth it to be uncomfortable at GlogauAIR if that's the ONLY way for you to stay in Berlin. callInfo.name: Rolling Three-Month Residency in Berlin
callInfo.description: Three-month residency for international artists in Berlin's Kreuzberg neighborhood. Private studio + accommodation; ~25 artists per year. Monthly open studios, exhibitions, salons. Rolling applications.

callInfo.name: International Residency 2026–27
callInfo.description: One- to two-month residencies in a former industrial complex in Barreiro, on the south bank of the Tagus opposite Lisbon. €1,550/month covers studio, accommodation, a program of activities, a final group exhibition, and professional documentation. Periods run through 2026 and into 2027.

callInfo.name: 2027 Rome Prize
callInfo.description: About 30 fellowships in the arts and humanities for a half-term (five months) or full-term (about eleven months) on the Academy's campus on the Janiculum in Rome. Fellows receive a stipend ($16,000 half-term / $30,000 full-term), room, board, and a study or studio. The 2027 application portal opens in August 2026; deadline November 1, 2026. Open to U.S. citizens and permanent residents.

callInfo.name: 2027 Studios of Key West Residency
callInfo.description: Two- to four-week residencies in a renovated historic armory in Key West, FL, for visual artists, writers, composers, and scholars. ~80 residents per year; private studios, apartments, and a busy schedule of communal events.

callInfo.name: 2027 ACRE Summer Sessions
callInfo.description: Two-week residencies on a rural property in Steuben, Wisconsin, hosted by a Chicago-based artist collective. ~30 artists per session for peer critique, performance nights, and lectures.

callInfo.name: 2028 Winter/Spring Residency at Caldera
callInfo.description: One-month residency for ~25 artists at Caldera Arts Center on Blue Lake in the Cascade Mountains of central Oregon. Disciplines include visual art, music composition, writing, film, performance, and interdisciplinary practice. Private cabin, weeknight communal meals, studio time, and a stipend. Annual deadline in May for the following winter/spring cycle.

callInfo.name: Rolling Residency at Flux Factory
callInfo.description: Studio + housing for emerging artists working in experimental, collaborative, and interdisciplinary practices. Multiple residency tracks of 3–12 months. Long Island City, Queens.

callInfo.description: Month-long residency in a former thrift store / living museum in downtown Greensboro, NC. Three-floor environment of accumulated objects from 1939–1997 that residents use as both studio and exhibition space. Interdisciplinary, collaborative, queer-friendly.

Three sessions of one hour per day: thirty-four days, the same routine: breakfast-write-walk to the office-write-lunch-walk to the office-write. The house is a dream. reviews.name: Chalk Hill Residency is a jewel
reviews.body: Chalk Hill Residency is a jewel. As a plein air landscape painter, the expansive property offered a myriad of places to paint - from vineyards to mountains to cliffs and the banks of the Russian river. The studio was a great place to keep supplies, and rest in the shade. The residence house is rustic and charming and art-filled. reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: Endless treasures to this residency
reviews.body:
Endless treasures to this residency. Old ranch houses, barns full of books, the lake with a small canoe, the river, lizards, rocks, chirping insect evenings to contemplate the work of the day, the friendliness of environment, pleasant solitude and closeness to the landscape. It was my first residency and such a very special place. The month passed with great speed....and wonderful and focused progress.

— Anonymous, 2015. Imported from the original ratemyartistresidency.com archive.

callInfo.description: Residency on a winery property in the Chalk Hill AVA of Sonoma County, California. Partners with non-profits, galleries, and museums; the winery + surrounding agricultural community is the working context.

The environment is serious as well as social; you make the residency what you wish it to be. The directors work very hard to make sure every resident has adequate equipment and what they need to make their work and feel comfortable all while being infectiously positive. Keep an eye out for upcoming open calls! www.cactroy.org

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: My time at Rivendell was the most productive, spiritual, and peaceful
reviews.body:
My time at Rivendell was the most productive, spiritual, and peaceful experience of my entire life. This serene setting offers incredible dwellings, a sincere reverence, and immeasurable kindness from the most compassionate hosts imaginable (Michael and Carmen). It's the kind of place you carry with you when you go, and I'm grateful Rivendell will always be a part of me.

— Anonymous, 2016. Imported from the original ratemyartistresidency.com archive.

reviews.author: Anonymous Artist
reviews.name: Rivendell was everything I thought it would be and so much more
reviews.body:
Rivendell was everything I thought it would be and so much more. I went into the weekend with high expectations, and the experience surpassed them all. The food, prepared for by a marvelous cook, was delicious! The staff was very helpful. The accommodations were cozy and allowed me to focus on my writing. The site, near serene ponds and atop the Cumberland Plateau, was beautiful. The workshop, led by two knowledgeable writers, was very informative. Needless to say, I cannot wait to go back!

callInfo.description:
2027
SPRING session: Mon, Mar 29th to Sat, May 22nd
FALL session: Mon, Sep 20th to Sat, Nov 13th
APPLY by November 1st, 2026

Read the full program description and apply here: https://salmoncreekfarm-arts.org/Schools-of-Salmon-Creek

Schools of Salmon Creek is a FREE two month land-based student-run school for artists *of all kinds* offered every spring and fall at Salmon Creek Farm. 

We carry on the legacy of the original counter-culture commune to this next chapter on the land by considering abundance, care-taking, climate, community, ecology, embodiment, habitat, inter-dependence, mystery, resilience, resourcefulness, self-sufficiency, sensuality, shelter, sustenance, and stewardship; getting off screens and out of doors; where the teachers are the land and each other.

For artists seeking a deeper connection to the natural world as a context for their work while engaging with other artists - we offer time, space, community, and the opportunity to participate in the daily life of the Salmon Creek Farm sanctuary on the Mendocino Coast. It is a good place to step away from daily routines and surrender to the cycles of life close to the land as part of an improvised artist community.

This is a space for active engagement, with the land and each other, not a residency to bring work in process, nor a conventional school where artists produce work alone in a studio. There are no typical indoor facilities or production spaces, just a desk in your private cabin, the triangle Dance Deck, the Outdoor Kitchen, the orchards & gardens, the riparian valley of Salmon Creek, and 33 acres of coast redwoods.
